findings.reason: The protected source uses a deque of allocatable numbers plus a direct availability table. Allocation, membership checks, exhaustion, safe release, and redundant release are all expressed plainly, and the two structures preserve a simple one-copy pool invariant. No candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 379 and its Python PhoneDirectory surface. The Reference defines the app-local operation-stream adapter without changing the native class semantics and preserves the three methods, arbitrary available-number choice, exhaustion result, source example, explanation sequence, and all three constraints.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064645618. Its deque initialization, availability flags, get, check, and release behavior are preserved exactly in the protected app-local class; solve is only the required deterministic operation-stream adapter.

The legal 64, 512, and 4096 tiers span 64x in directory capacity and allocation count, exercising the path that distinguishes constant-time pool removal from repeated scans. The current source passes all 11 executions at -0.01 relative growth and 1.00x; a correct list.index allocator passes every benchmark output but fails only scaling at +0.32.

The Approach accurately describes queue allocation, direct availability checks, idempotent release, the synchronization invariant, arbitrary allocation order, O(1) time per public operation, and O(maxNumbers) storage.

The hash-bound Premium Reference remains source-fidelity verified, including the full operation contract, the sole source example and its complete eight-step behavior, valid number range, capacity limit, and total-call limit.

coverage: The sole authenticated Premium source example now appears first as the complete seven-operation app trace, including release(2) and the final successful check that were previously missing.

A one-number directory covers minimum capacity, repeated exhaustion, and reuse; source and trial checks cover both endpoint numbers, while generated validation covers maxNumbers=10000 and the 20000-call limit.
Initial availability, allocation, stable exhaustion, allocation checks, release checks, middle-pool reuse, and redundant release exercise every public state transition.

Authored outputs and runtime outputs were validated independently because get may choose any available number; an independent queue/flag model also verified 23,878 exhaustive streams and 10,000 random suites.
All eight correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged 64-, 512-, and 4,096-allocation workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
